issues.body: `container`/`boundBy` gives each node a single owner, and `scopedNodes` consequently emits its class and attributes only under the first OPTIONAL or FILTER NOT EXISTS that reaches it. With `?person OPTIONAL worksAt ?org` and `?company OPTIONAL partnerOf ?org`, where `?org a ex:Organisation`, the second OPTIONAL can bind `?org` to a non-Organisation whenever the first does not bind it. Likewise, the mixed OPTIONAL/NOT EXISTS case excludes any partner rather than only a partner satisfying the target node constraints. This changes query answers and contradicts the canvas node's shared type/attribute semantics.
issues.fix_hint: Emit the shared target's constraints in every scoped incoming group that can independently bind or test that target, while avoiding top-level hoisting. For the two-OPTIONAL case, both OPTIONAL blocks should contain `?organisation a ex:Organisation`; the exclusion block should contain the same target constraints. Replace the current expected-string tests with those expectations and add result-equivalence fixtures where the second edge reaches a non-matching target, so the tests fail if constraints are omitted.
issues.title: Shared scoped targets apply node constraints to only the first incoming group

issues.body: The two new shared-target tests explicitly expect the target type triple only in the first OPTIONAL and absent from the second OPTIONAL or exclusion. Those assertions pass the flawed single-owner implementation but do not verify that every binding path respects the typed node. They are therefore non-vacuous serialization tests of the wrong invariant, not result-equivalence evidence.
issues.fix_hint: Expect the target class and attribute patterns in each independently scoped group, and execute the generated query against data containing both matching and non-matching target types to pin the intended answer set for two OPTIONALs and OPTIONAL plus FILTER NOT EXISTS.
issues.title: Shared-target tests codify incomplete semantics instead of checking answers

verdict.summary: Round 3 replaces the degree heuristic and correctly nests chained OPTIONAL patterns, but shared typed targets are still serialized with incomplete constraints. The new ownership model assigns a node's class and attributes to only the first scoped edge that reaches it. A later OPTIONAL can therefore bind that same variable without satisfying the node's declared type or attributes, and a later FILTER NOT EXISTS tests a broader pattern than the diagram describes. The new exact-string tests encode this incorrect behavior rather than establishing result equivalence. The prior major scoping defect therefore remains at the same severity.
